title: Karyalay Mail event envelope v1
description: The shared envelope every Karyalay event carries, transcribed from Master Contract §22.3. No repository redefines it. `data` is constrained by the per-event payload schema named in events/catalog-v1.yaml; this schema deliberately leaves it open so the envelope can be validated independently of any one event.
$comment: Consumer semantics (Master §22.2, Repo 1 §31.2): delivery is at-least-once and the same event_id may be redelivered after a broker acknowledgement that the producer failed to record. Handlers MUST be idempotent on event_id. Ordering is guaranteed only where documented for a resource; compare resource.generation when order matters. Poison events go to dead-letter with alerting, never silent deletion.

event.description: Lower-case dotted past-tense fact name (Master §22.4). Command-style names are not events.

version.description: Event schema major version. An unknown version is routed to a compatibility error/alert, never parsed as an older version (Repo 1 Appendix D.1).

event_id.description: UUIDv7 (RFC 9562, Master §6.2). Also the NATS Nats-Msg-Id and the consumer deduplication key. Never overloaded with request_id, trace_id or an idempotency key (Master §6.2).

occurred_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant the fact was committed (Master §20.2).

trace_id.description: W3C trace context trace-id carried across the outbox hop (Master §30.1, §20.7).

request_id.description: Correlation ID of the request that caused the fact (Master §6.3, §20.7). Null for scheduler-originated facts.

organisation_id.description: Tenant the fact belongs to (Master §6.3). Null only for security/platform events that belong to no customer (Master §22.3).

resource.description: The aggregate the fact is about (Master §22.3).

generation.description: Desired revision of the resource (Master §6.2). Present for every resource that participates in reconciliation; null for those that do not. Consumers compare it when ordering matters (Master §22.2).

data.description: Event payload. MUST NOT carry message bodies, attachment contents, passwords, app-password secrets or private cryptographic keys (Master §22.5, Repo 1 §31.3).
